hook: Peter Thiel co-founded PayPal, led it as chief executive and took it public before eBay bought it in 2002. He then co-founded Palantir Technologies, the data analytics company he chairs, and in 2005 started Founders Fund, where he is a partner. He made the first outside investment in Facebook and started the Thiel Fellowship, which funds young people who leave or skip college to build new things.

quick_facts: Born in Frankfurt am Main, West Germany, in 1967, he holds a philosophy degree and a law degree from Stanford University.
Before PayPal he clerked for a federal appeals judge, practised securities law at Sullivan & Cromwell and traded currency options at Credit Suisse.
He co-founded PayPal in 1998 with Max Levchin and Luke Nosek and remained chief executive through its $1.5 billion sale to eBay in 2002.
In 2004 he made the first outside investment in Facebook, $500,000, and sat on the board of the company, later Meta Platforms, until 2022.
Founders Fund lists him as a partner and as chairman of Palantir Technologies, which was incorporated in 2003.
He co-wrote Zero to One, a 2014 book on start-ups drawn from a class he taught at Stanford, with Blake Masters.
